name: Grouper
label: Kranky
lede: Liz Harris grew up in a commune called The Group, took her stage name from what the kids there called each other, and has recorded under tape hiss thick enough that a microwave beep and a fever both ended up on the records.

eras.title: A childhood inside The Group
eras.text: Liz Harris was born in West Marin, California, in 1980 and raised around the Bay Area in a Fourth Way commune built on the teachings of George Gurdjieff. She studied art at UC Berkeley and worked with Mayo Thompson at the Patrick Painter gallery in Los Angeles before the music took over.

years.h: Liz Harris grows up in a Gurdjieff commune where everyone is a grouper
years.p: Harris was raised in a Fourth Way commune the members called The Group. The kids there called each other and their parents "groupers", and she took the word for her project.
years.xp:
Harris told an interviewer that growing up there was "us making our own identities inside a pretty controlled environment, and sort of lashing back maybe." The word was a small defiance.

When she started recording, it fit a second way: she has described the music as at its barest just a grouping of sounds, with herself as the grouper.

eras.title: Tape hiss in Portland
eras.text: Working out of Portland, Oregon, Harris put out CD-Rs and small-label records of guitar, voice and loops smeared into fog. The UK label Type picked her up, and Dragging a Dead Deer Up a Hill was the record where people started hearing the songs inside.

years.h: Harris self-releases a CD-R, then Way Their Crept
years.p: The debut Grouper comes out as a CD-R in 2005. Way Their Crept follows, and the UK label Type reissues it in 2007.

years.h: A third album, and a record with Xiu Xiu
years.p: Wide is the third Grouper album. Creepshow is the collaboration with [[Xiu Xiu|8b431ac6-0806-4e4a-9b6b-1734370fa890]].

years.h: One more album of drones and half-heard vocals
years.p: Cover the Windows and the Walls is the last Grouper record before the one that changed things.

years.src: Wikipedia: Dragging a Dead Deer Up a Hill · Wikipedia: Grouper (musician)
years.h: Songs surface through the haze on Dragging a Dead Deer Up a Hill
years.p: The cover is a childhood photo of Harris taken by her mother. Stereogum later called it her first set of songs that sound like songs.
years.xp:
Pitchfork's Mike McGonigal gave it 8.2 and called it an arresting album of pastoral psychedelic pop. AllMusic's Heather Phares heard "more melody, more structured songs, and even a few phrases emerge from the ether."

Ten years on, Pitchfork put it at No. 6 on its list of the best dream pop albums. Kranky reissued it in 2013.
play: Dragging a Dead Deer Up a Hill

eras.title: She starts a label and writes for sleep
eras.text: Grouper started her own label, Yellow Electric, for a two-part album, then pushed into long tape collages and an eight-hour piece shaped like a night's sleep. Her first Kranky release came through a duo with Tiny Vipers' Jesy Fortino.

years.cap: Liz Harris at the Empty Bottle, Chicago, September 30, 2011
years.src: Wikipedia: A I A: Alien Observer
years.h: A I A comes in two halves, on Harris's own label
years.p: Dream Loss and Alien Observer are the first records on Yellow Electric. Alien Observer comes out April 11 and Pitchfork later ranked it 21st among the best ambient albums ever.
years.xp:
The single Alien Observer came out April 3, 2011, eight days ahead of the album. The record runs 39 minutes and 7 seconds over seven tracks; the longest, Vapor Trails, is 9:05. Pitchfork gave it 8.1.

Pitchfork's Kevin Lozano wrote that "Liz Harris' voice has the ability to leave you dumbstruck, speechless, just plain wrecked."

years.h: Two musicians who toured Europe together become Mirrorring
years.p: Harris and Tiny Vipers' [[Jesy Fortino|e37d27dd-7d69-4f60-964b-397669364841]] spell the name with a doubled r for symmetry. Foreign Body is Harris's first album on Kranky.
years.xp: The duo came out of that European tour, and both kept their main projects going. Foreign Body came out in March 2012 and was reviewed by Pitchfork, Drowned in Sound, AllMusic and PopMatters.

years.h: Eight hours long, shaped like one night's sleep
years.p: With [[Jefre Cantu-Ledesma|9b69c184-919f-4db2-a2a4-995024f69334]], Harris premieres Circular Veil at Berlin's Club Transmediale, designed to mimic one full sleep cycle.
years.xp: The same year she toured the UK and Europe with Violet Replacement, a set of long tape collage pieces.

eras.title: Kranky, and the piano record from Portugal
eras.text: Now on Kranky, Grouper put out an album of old outtakes, then a piano record made in a borrowed house in Portugal. Ruins became her most acclaimed album, and she branched into film, an opera-house commission and curating a festival.

years.cap: Grouper at OBEY Convention VI, Halifax, June 2013
years.src: Wikipedia: The Man Who Died in His Boat
years.h: Harris looks inside a wrecked sailboat, then names an album for it
years.p: The Man Who Died in His Boat is Grouper's first solo Kranky album, built from outtakes of the Dragging a Dead Deer sessions. The wreck washed up at Agate Beach in Bolinas.
years.xp:
Harris walked down with her father to look inside the cabin and said she felt she was violating what was left of the man by witnessing it. According to Wikipedia, the boat likely belonged to Dr. William Groppe, whose fully provisioned sailboat was found off Agate Beach in August 1998; he was declared dead in absentia that October while sailing for Hawaii.

Pitchfork named the single Vital a Best New Track. Kranky also reissued Dragging a Dead Deer Up a Hill and the A I A albums that year.

years.h: A microwave beeps in Portugal, and Harris leaves it on Ruins
years.p: Harris recorded Ruins in 2011 during a residency in Aljezur, Portugal, on a portable 4-track and an upright piano. When a storm cut the power, a microwave beeped, and she kept it at the end of Labyrinth.
years.xp: The house belonged to the aunt of music director Sérgio Hydalgo; the residency was organized by Galeria Zé dos Bois. The last track was recorded separately at her mother's house in 2004. Pitchfork gave Ruins Best New Music and ranked it the fifth best album of 2014.

years.h: Harris sings on The Bug's Angels & Devils
years.p: She sings on Void and Black Wasp for [[Kevin Martin|ac853422-64b8-493f-96cd-3eb0b209b8aa]]'s The Bug, and starts the trio Helen with Jed Bindeman and Scott Simmons.
Leeds' Opera North asks Harris and San Francisco filmmaker Paul Clipson for a live film-and-music piece. Helen releases The Original Faces the same year.

years.h: Le Guess Who? hands its 11th edition to Harris
years.p: Grouper programs [[William Basinski|3b731282-d7f4-41a5-af0a-d0c1c3319802]], Keiji Haino and Richard Youngs, plus Kieślowski's The Double Life of Véronique and Paul Clipson's Lighthouse.

eras.title: Short, then fifteen years at once
eras.text: Grouper's next Kranky record is an album she stopped making when she got sick, and she wouldn't pad it. The one after collects songs from fifteen years of recording. In between she releases music under a new name.

years.src: Wikipedia: Grid of Points · Wikipedia: Grouper (musician)
years.h: A fever ends Grid of Points at 22 minutes
years.p: Liz Harris wrote and recorded it in about a week and a half at the Ucross Foundation in Wyoming in 2014, snowed in, until a fever stopped her. Kranky worried it was too short; she wouldn't add anything.
years.xp: The first single, Parking Lot, arrived on March 8, 2018, and was named one of NPR's Songs We Love and a Pitchfork Best New Track. The album runs 21 minutes and 52 seconds and scored 80 on Metacritic.

years.p: After Its Own Death / Walking in a Spiral Towards the House comes out on her Yellow Electric label, her first major work outside the Grouper name.

yt: Full set, Bourse du Commerce, Paris, 2022
years.p: Announced with the single Unclean Mind on July 27, 2021, Grouper's Kranky album collects songs Harris recorded over the previous fifteen years.

years.h: Nine years on, Raum comes back with Daughter
years.p: Harris and [[Jefre Cantu-Ledesma|9b69c184-919f-4db2-a2a4-995024f69334]] release a second Raum album after The Event of Your Leaving. Harris now lives in Astoria, Oregon, where she runs an exhibition space.
